text.title: Checkpoint Ledger Spec — Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces: a Checkpoint Ledger Spec as YAML or JSON, describing one orchestrator's state directory, marker vocabulary, write boundaries and recovery operations. Machine-checkable by the bundled validator.

section.title: State directory layout
section.statement: The spec describes this shape and the validator assumes it: `<state_root>/<unit_id>/` containing `meta.txt` (identity and provenance, written once at enrol), `phase-<name>.in-flight` / `.done` / `.failed` (derived status, one file per phase reached), and `history.log` (append-only record). `<state_root>` is gitignored: it is run state, not source.

contract.field: Which orchestrator this specifies, in one line.
Directory holding one subdirectory per unit.
Must be `true`. Run state in version control produces merge conflicts on every tick.
Regex every unit id must match. The identity guard rejects anything else before it can create a phantom unit (r1).
Ordered phase names, earliest first. Rollback truncates in this order; the order is the only thing that makes "at or after" meaningful.
The ONE command that creates a state directory. Any other writer must fail on a missing directory (r1).
The marker writer. Must be distinct from `enrol_command`.
Must be `false`. This is the ghost-state guard stated as a field so it can be checked (r1).
Exactly `in-flight`, `done`, `failed`. `rolled-back` is a history verb, not a marker — a rolled-back phase has no marker at all (r5).
Must be `before_dispatch` (r2).
Filename of the append-only log, relative to the unit directory.
Must contain `iso_ts`, `phase`, `status` and a reason or commit token (r3).
The mutual-exclusion mechanism guarding appends — e.g. `flock on <state_root>/.lock`.

Must contain all four of `identity`, `snapshot`, `provenance`, `status`. Identity is what the unit is; snapshot is what state it reached; provenance is what produced it (commit, model, brief); status is where it stands.

Closed vocabulary: `model_call`, `non_idempotent_side_effect`, `risky_step`, `human_gate`. `model_call` is always required; the other three are required whenever the matching `has_*` flag is true (r4).
Does the run commit, push, publish, pay or send?
Does any phase wait on a person?
Must take a unit and a phase. Truncate-and-requeue, never retry-in-place (r5).
Age at which an `in-flight` marker is swept. Must exceed the longest expected phase, not the average one (r6).
How the sweep proves the agent is gone before acting. A timer alone is not a liveness check.
Must be `false`. Stale markers go to dead-letter and wait for an operator (r6).
Must be `false`. A packaged tool may scaffold and unpack; it may not advance a run (r7).

section.title: Consistency rules the validator enforces
section.statement: `lineage` entries are unique and non-empty; every phase named in `write_boundaries` context, in `rollback_command` examples, or in the template must resolve to a lineage entry. `marker_states` equals the three-value set exactly — an extra state such as `skipped` or `partial` is rejected, because each additional state doubles the recovery matrix and the ones that get added are always derivable from the history. `in_flight_written`, `mark_creates_dirs`, `auto_redispatch_on_stale`, `cli_writes_checkpoints` and `gitignored` each have exactly one permitted value; they exist as fields precisely so the guard is stated rather than assumed.
